text:
maya: Heads up — I'm starting a canary for the quota-aware routing change. pushing config to region-us-west, 2% of traffic. want to watch cost vs latency signals :eyes:
jon: thx. can you paste the config snippet? want to sanity-check weights and fallbacks
zara: quick note: console previews currently hide quota allocation details. ops asked for a per-route breakdown before we widen rollout
maya: snippet:
```json
{"routing_policy":"quota_aware","buckets":[{"id":"primary","share":0.98},{"id":"backup","share":0.02}],"quota_threshold":{"tokens_per_min":10000},"fallback":"legacy_route"}
```
sam: looks fine but we need a throttling guard if quota errors spike. otherwise clients will see 429/500 churn
jon: agreed. propose adding a soft-failover: if error_rate > 0.8% over 5m OR latency_p95 > 800ms then route 100% to legacy for 15m
maya: adding that to the canary controller now. question: should failover be instantaneous or smoothed to avoid flapping?
zara: smooth it — 10s step-down with a cooldown of 2m. also add a note in the console UI: "automatic failover engaged" with a link to the incident event
maya: yep. will wire in event annotation to the route timeline.
deploy-bot: Canary deployment started by maya: canary_id=canary-1876543210 region=us-west traffic=2%
infra-audit-bot: Audit log: config.upsert user=maya id=canary-1876543210 at=2026-03-18T15:12:30Z
sam: telemetry question — are we sampling full request traces for the canary? need traces to validate root-cause of latency regressions
jon: let's sample 10% traces for canary traffic and tag with canary_id. also emit per-token cost metric to the route telemetry pipeline
maya: done. also created a dashboard panel: Dashboards > Routing > canary-1876543210 (link: https://dashboards.redwood.internal/routing/canary-1876543210)
zara: UX follow-up: console should show planned rollout plan (2% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100%) and allow manual step / abort. right now it's implicit in the playbook text
maya: noted. filing a small UX ticket for show-rollout-steps and expanded telemetry lines: https://jira.redwood.com/browse/ENGPLAT-1429
sam: edge case: what about long-lived streaming connections? quota-aware routing might rebalance mid-stream and break sessions
jon: good catch. for streaming we should sticky-route by connection_id and only rebalance on reconnect or explicit migrate. add `sticky_sessions: true` to the policy for streaming routes
maya: patched config and re-deployed canary.
deploy-bot: Health check: canary-1876543210 region=us-west status=healthy (latency_p95=210ms, error_rate=0.02%)
zara: running a small A/B eval set against golden prompts — early quality checks look neutral. keep watching rerank+chat outputs for degeneration
sam: if anything odd, plan to set traffic back to 0% and roll forward a non-quota variant
maya: agreed. timeline: we'll watch for 6h at 2% with 10% trace sampling then step to 5% if stable. abort criteria: error_rate > 0.8% OR p95 latency up > 200ms OR cost_per_request +10% vs baseline
jon: logging the abort criteria into the canary controller config. also added a dry-run toggle so we can preview decisions in console without changing traffic
zara: can we surface the dry-run results in the rollout timeline UI? that would help the product folks
maya: will add API for dry-run events; UX ticket updated to include dry-run visualization
infra-audit-bot: Audit log: policy.trigger user=jon action=update canary=canary-1876543210 at=2026-03-18T15:22:11Z
sam: small nit — the console toast for "automatic failover engaged" should include the snapshot id so oncall can inspect config state quickly
maya: yep putting snapshot id in event payload
jon: sweet. thanks everyone. if we don't see issues in 6h, i'll bump to 5% then ping oncall for another sanity check
zara: thanks — great coordination :thumbsup:
